name: Thunderbird
hook: The 20-year veteran of email, now on Android — one unified inbox for every account, push notifications, and zero ads or trackers.
bullets: Unified inbox that folds Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo, and any IMAP account into one view
Push notifications via IMAP IDLE — mail arrives without polling the battery dry
OpenPGP encryption built in, no separate plugin to install
The codebase is k-9 Mail, now maintained as the official Thunderbird for Android
benefits: Every account in one place — check mail once, not app by app
Backed by the Thunderbird project: audited, ad-free, and tracking-free by design
Sign in with OAuth or an app password; no proprietary sync service required
Conversations, stars, search, and folders behave like desktop Thunderbird
setupSteps: Install Thunderbird from F-Droid, Play Store, or the project's GitHub releases
Add each account — sign in with OAuth where your provider supports it
Switch on the unified inbox to see all accounts in one stream
Tune per-account notifications so only what matters buzzes your phone
details: Thunderbird for Android is the official mobile client from the Thunderbird project, born from the merger of the long-running k-9 Mail and Thunderbird desktop lineages. It handles IMAP, POP3, and Exchange accounts with OAuth sign-in, pushes new mail through IMAP IDLE instead of scheduled polling, and folds any number of accounts into a single unified inbox. Conversations, unified folders, full-text search, and per-account identities behave like the desktop app, and OpenPGP encryption is built in through Autocrypt — no plugin to hunt down. The app is Apache-2.0 licensed, contains no ads or analytics, and ships in over 20 languages. Like its desktop sibling, it is a pure email client: your address stays with your provider, and Thunderbird never sees your mail on a server of its own.
setup: App (Android) — sign in to your accounts
